data.field_of_study: Development Policy and Politics; relevant social science and related degrees (e.g. Social Policy, Sociology, Politics, International Relations, Development Studies)
data.other_hard: domiciled or permanent resident in an African country; under 30 years of age at the time of applying; IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL 580/93 required for applicants whose first language is not English; first degree in a listed relevant subject
data.evidence_sentence: Applicants must be African nationals domiciled (or permanent residents) in an African country.
data.notes: Page is outdated: it states applications for 2026 entry are closed and gives no deadline for later entry. Preference (not requirement) for candidates living in Sub-Saharan Africa. Applicants who are nationals or domiciled in Sudan or Cameroon should refer to the government website, which is not described on this page. Scholarship is for a two-year programme: one-year MSc plus a one-year integrated internship (six months at the University, six months with the Mo Ibrahim Foundation in London). Page mentions an arrival allowance of £1,082 and says the internship is funded directly by the Foundation, but does not state tuition coverage, so funding type is uncertain. Page says a first class degree is essential; anyone not meeting this will not be considered.
